content: Dr. Haroon Saloojee is a Senior Lecturer in the Department of Obstetrics and Gynaecology at the University of Nairobi, Kenya. Dr. Sadia Shakoor serves as an Associate Professor in Pathology and Laboratory Medicine, as well as Pediatrics and Child Health, at Aga Khan University in Karachi, Pakistan. Dr. Rachel Smith is a Senior Midwifery Advisor at the Burnet Institute in Melbourne, Australia. Dr. Joseph S. Solomkin is the Executive Director of OASIS Global, based in Cincinnati, Ohio, USA. Observers include Deborah Armbruster, a Senior Maternal and Newborn Health Advisor at the United States Agency for International Development (USAID) in Washington, D.C., and Emma Clark, a Senior Maternal Health Advisor contracted by USAID. Dr. Jeanne A. Conry, President-elect of the International Federation of Gynecology and Obstetrics (FIGO) and Past President of the American College of Obstetrics and Gynecology, is based in California, USA. Dr. Maria Fernanda Escobar, a FIGO representative and Obstetrician/Gynaecologist, is affiliated with Fundación Valle del Lili in Cali, Colombia. Dr. Jeff Smith is the Deputy Director of Implementation Research and Demonstration for Scale in Maternal, Newborn, and Child Health at the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation in Seattle, Washington, USA. Ann Yates is the Lead Midwifery Advisor for the International Confederation of Midwifery in The Hague, Netherlands. The Evidence Synthesis Group (ESG) includes Dr. Edgardo Abalos, Vice Director of Centro Rosarino de Estudios Perinatales in Rosario, Argentina, and Anna Cuthbert from the Cochrane Pregnancy and Childbirth Group in Liverpool, United Kingdom. Other members include Virginia Diaz, Katherine Eddy, Leanne Jones, Frances Kellie, and Myfanwy Williams, all of whom are affiliated with the Cochrane Pregnancy and Childbirth Group at the University of Liverpool. The External Review Group (ERG) features Dr. Ayse Akin from the Department of Public Health at Baskent University in Ankara, Turkey, and Dr. Justus Hofmeyr from the Department of Obstetrics and Gynaecology at the University of Botswana and the University of the Witwatersrand in South Africa. Dr. Tina Lavender, from the Centre for Global Women’s Health at the University of Manchester, and Dr. Suneeta Mittal, from the Department of Obstetrics and Gynaecology at Fortis Memorial Research Institute in India, are also members. Dr. Alan Tita, from the Maternal-Fetal Medicine Division at the University of Alabama at Birmingham, and Dr. Khalid Yunis, Professor of Pediatrics and Head of Neonatology at the American University of Beirut, are included as well. Dr. John Varallo, Global Director of Safe Surgery at Jhpiego, an affiliate of Johns Hopkins University, is based in Baltimore, Maryland, USA. WHO country and regional officers include Bremen De Mucio (WHO Regional Office of the Americas, Uruguay), Karima Gholbzouri (WHO Regional Office for Eastern Mediterranean, Egypt), Chandani Anoma Jayathilaka (WHO Regional Office for South-East Asia, India), Oleg Kuzmenko (WHO Regional Office for Europe, Denmark), Leopold Ouedraogo (WHO Regional Office for Africa, Congo), and Howard Sobel (WHO Regional Office for the Western Pacific, Philippines). The WHO Steering Group includes Dr. Mercedes Bonet, Dr. Doris Chou, Dr. Tina Lavin, Dr. Olufemi T. Oladapo, Dr. Joshua P. Vogel, and Dr. Maurice Bucagu, all of whom are involved in maternal and perinatal health research. Christine Francis, a consultant in infection prevention and control, is also part of the team. The WHO recommendation on prophylactic antibiotics for women undergoing cesarean section prioritizes critical outcomes such as severe infectious morbidity (e.g., sepsis, septic shock, laparotomy, hysterectomy, or ICU admission), puerperal infections (e.g., endometritis, myometritis, salpingitis), wound infections, side effects of antibiotics, and antimicrobial resistance. Important outcomes include maternal death, maternal well-being, maternal satisfaction, cost of care, neonatal mortality, and neonatal infections. The evidence synthesis is based on a Cochrane systematic review of 39 trials, with data from 33 trials involving 8,073 women. The review compares the effectiveness of different antibiotic classes in preventing post-operative infections. Key comparisons include anti-staphylococcal cephalosporins versus broad-spectrum penicillins, minimally anti-staphylococcal cephalosporins versus non-anti-staphylococcal penicillins, and other combinations. The findings highlight the need for targeted antibiotic use to address the principal causative agents of infection, including Gram-positive cocci, anaerobes, and Gram-negative bacilli. The review emphasizes the importance of evidence-based decision-making in selecting antibiotics for cesarean section prophylaxis, considering both clinical efficacy and the potential for antimicrobial resistance.
